$comment: Candidate SemanticScopeDescriptor. Normative text: SPEC_SEMANTIC_SCOPE_DESCRIPTOR.md; the profile it projects: ../texture/SPEC_UVT.md. Status is `candidate`: this descriptor exists so a UVT materialization can name the scope its receipt was taken under, and its hashes are admission-only evidence. It is not a release or compatibility guarantee, and it carries no conformance vectors yet — the second independent texture path that would justify them does not exist.
summary: The texture semantic plane a live raster projection and a materialized-then-reopened UVT projection must reproduce exactly: container topology, colour and alpha semantics, orientation and the sampler a runtime should bind.

envelope.facets: ordered [facetKey, value] pairs for every present facet
envelope.absentFacets: ordered facetKey list for every optional facet the publisher did not publish

numeric.model: IEEE-754 binary64 only; the canonical form encodes every number as its 16 hex-digit big-endian bit pattern, so integers and reals share one representation
numeric.float32Widening: float32 source values widen to binary64 exactly; no rounding, no requantisation. Only atlas pivots are non-integral in this scope
numeric.nonFinite: NaN, +Infinity and -Infinity are rejected; a projection that would produce one is a diagnostic, never a hash
numeric.comparison: equality is byte equality of the canonical encoding; no epsilon and no tolerance exists in this scope

missingSemantics.absentFacet: an optional facet the publisher did not publish; it is named in absentFacets and contributes its key, never a fabricated value
missingSemantics.absentKey: forbidden inside a facet value: every key declared by the facet is always present
missingSemantics.null: used for exactly one member, `swizzle`, which a container may genuinely not carry. A KTXswizzle entry that is absent is null and never an invented «rgba»
missingSemantics.empty: an empty atlas region list is not representable: a projection with no regions omits the atlas facet entirely, because the profile requires at least one region wherever the block exists
missingSemantics.unknown: this scope defines no unknown sentinel. A source whose colour space, alpha mode or orientation is unknown cannot be projected at all — the profile admits linear|srgb, opaque|straight|premultiplied and rd|ru, and guessing any of the three changes every pixel's meaning

ordering.facets: by facetKey in UTF-8 byte order
ordering.absentFacets: by facetKey in UTF-8 byte order
ordering.objectKeys: by UTF-8 byte order of the key, applied by the canonical form itself
ordering.atlasRegions: by region id in UTF-8 byte order; ids are unique within a projection
ordering.sequences: a region's x/y/width/height and its pivot keep their declared component order: they are coordinates, not a set

resourceClosure.policy: no-closure: a UVT projection is a single self-contained container plus its sidecar

modes.logical: not used by this scope; a texture projection references nothing outside its own container, so there is no logical identity to carry
modes.content-qualified: not used by this scope; the artifact digest of the container is the receipt's business, not a facet's

resourceClosure.modeIsHashedRationale: stated for schema conformity; this scope publishes no closure facet at all, so no mode can be selected and none can be confused with another
resourceClosure.digestForm: <algorithm>:<lowercase hex>; a bare hex string is rejected

facets.summary: The KTX 2.0 header fields the UVT sidecar copies verbatim, never normalised.

keys.vkFormat: integer >= 0, the container's own header value
keys.pixelDepth: integer, 0 for the 2D and array/cube topologies this profile admits
keys.layerCount: integer >= 0, 0 for a plain image; copied verbatim rather than normalised to 1
keys.levelCount: integer >= 1; KTX2 encodes «generate mips at load» as 0 and a normalized projection states what it contains

live.note: width/height/depth/layers/faces/mipLevels of RasterImageInfo, with layerCount carrying the container's 0-for-non-array convention rather than the source's 1

artifact.note: the eight header fields of the KTX 2.0 container, read back from the file itself

facets.summary: Colour, transfer, alpha and orientation semantics, which a runtime cannot recover from the pixels.

keys.premultipliedAlpha: boolean, the Data Format Descriptor flag
keys.alphaMode: opaque | straight | premultiplied; premultiplied requires premultipliedAlpha true and opaque forbids it
keys.orientation: rd | ru, KTXorientation in S-then-T form
keys.swizzle: four characters from rgba01, or null when the container carries no KTXswizzle entry

live.note: colorSpace maps to transferFunction and primaries, alphaMode maps to alphaMode and premultipliedAlpha, orientation maps top-left to rd and bottom-left to ru. `unknown` is not projectable in any of the three

artifact.note: the Data Format Descriptor's transfer function and alpha-premultiplied flag, the KTXorientation and KTXswizzle key/value entries, and the sidecar's own alphaMode

facets.summary: How a runtime should bind the texture. Advice the projection carries, required so no consumer has to guess.

keys.mipFilter: none | nearest | linear; anything but none requires levelCount > 1

live.note: no live raster contract publishes sampler state today: a decoded region says nothing about how a runtime should bind it. A projector therefore supplies the sampler, and the receipt records that it did — this null is why the scope is a candidate rather than registered

artifact.note: the sidecar's sampler block, which the profile requires

facets.summary: Named regions of the container that mean something on their own, with optional pivots.

keys.regions: array of { id, x, y, width, height, pivot: [number, number] | null }, ordered by id, each lying inside pixelWidth x pixelHeight

facets.presenceRule: present only when the projection declares at least one region; an atlas with no region is the absent facet, not an empty one

live.note: no live raster contract publishes atlas regions today; a sprite sheet is a UV-level fact a projector supplies, and the absence of a publisher is recorded here rather than hidden

liveBaseContract.note: the base contract the container and colour facets are computable from today, unchanged. The scope adds no member to it.

artifactProfile.marker: a KTX 2.0 container plus a `.uvt.json` sidecar whose `uv` block is { format: UVT, version: 1.0 }
artifactProfile.mandatoryMapping: every field of the sidecar's ktx2 block is a verbatim copy of a value that exists in the container; a sidecar that contradicts its container is a defect, not a preference (SPEC_UVT §1)
artifactProfile.levelData: level 0 only in this version: the profile carries a mip chain, and a projection built from one decoded region has one level. A source with more levels records the difference in its MaterializationReceipt

notFrozenHere: the pixels: this scope hashes the semantics a runtime needs in order to bind a texture correctly, not the image content. Two projections that agree on every facet may still hold different pictures, and the container's artifactCanonicalDigest is what distinguishes them.

the source-pixel-format to vkFormat conversion table: which Vulkan format a converter chooses for a given decoded region is a conversion decision belonging to that converter, and the profile deliberately leaves vkFormat unrestricted.

palette-indexed sources, animated frame sequences, per-product transcoding targets, 3D volume topology and the wider Khronos transfer set — each named in ../NOTES.md with the reason it is not specified yet.

compatibility.minorVersions: additive only: a new optional facet, a new accepted digest algorithm or a new enum value. A 1.0 consumer keeps computing 1.0 hashes and must refuse to compare them with a hash produced under a different scope version.
compatibility.majorVersions: may remove or redefine a facet. A consumer refuses a major it does not implement rather than guessing.
compatibility.hashComparability: two hashes are comparable only when scope id, scope version, the present facet set and the absent facet set all match. A candidate scope's hashes are admission-only evidence and are never a release compatibility claim.
